title: Gill Captains the Test. Kohli and Rohit Return for the ODIs. India’s Afghanistan Series Starts Friday.
excerpt: A Chandigarh Test, three ODIs across Dharamshala, Lucknow and Chennai, and a chance for NRIs to watch India’s next generation step up while the old guard returns for white-ball cricket.
body:
India’s first bilateral cricket series after IPL 2026 begins on Friday with a one-off Test against Afghanistan in Chandigarh. The tour, running from June 6 to June 20, features four matches across four cities and marks a significant moment for Indian cricket: the formal transition of Test leadership to the next generation while Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma prepare for what could be one of their final ODI campaigns.

Shubman Gill Leads the Test

The BCCI’s decision to hand Shubman Gill the Test captaincy against Afghanistan is the clearest signal yet about India’s future leadership plans. At twenty-six, Gill has already led India in limited-overs cricket and captained Gujarat Titans in the IPL. Now he gets a full Test match to make his case in red-ball cricket.

KL Rahul has been named vice-captain. The Test squad is built around youth and emerging talent: Yashasvi Jaiswal opens alongside Gill, Sai Sudharsan slots into the middle order, and Devdutt Padikkal returns to the setup after strong domestic performances. Rishabh Pant keeps wicket, with Dhruv Jurel as backup.

The bowling attack features Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna leading the pace department, with Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, and Manav Suthar providing spin options. The most notable absence is Jasprit Bumrah, who has been rested from both formats for workload management.

Kohli and Rohit Return for the ODIs

The three-match ODI series beginning June 14 in Dharamshala is where NRI cricket fans will want to pay closest attention. Both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return to international duty, having last played in the T20 World Cup in February. Since retiring from Tests and T20Is, the fifty-over format is the only stage where these two batting legends still represent India.

The ODI squad also includes Shreyas Iyer, Hardik Pandya, Ishan Kishan, and Arshdeep Singh. The BCCI has noted that participation of senior players like Rohit and Hardik depends on fitness clearances before the fixtures.

For Kohli in particular, this series matters beyond runs. The England tour begins on July 1 with five T20Is and three ODIs, and the ODI leg against Afghanistan is the only competitive cricket he will play between the IPL and that tour.

Afghanistan Are No Pushovers

The visitors have named experienced squads under captain Hashmatullah Shahidi. The Test squad includes the returning Sediqullah Atal and Azmatullah Omarzai, while the ODI setup features Rashid Khan, Ibrahim Zadran, and Rahmanullah Gurbaz.

Afghanistan’s only previous Test against India ended in a heavy defeat in Bengaluru in 2018, but they have grown considerably since. In ODIs, their record against India includes a famous tied match in the 2018 Asia Cup and competitive performances in recent ICC events. Rashid Khan in Indian conditions, under lights in Dharamshala and Chennai, is a challenge no batting lineup should take lightly.

The Full Schedule

Test Match June 6–10 | Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Stadium, New Chandigarh | 9:30 AM IST

1st ODI June 14 | HPCA Stadium, Dharamshala | 1:30 PM IST

2nd ODI June 17 | Ekana Cricket Stadium, Lucknow | 1:30 PM IST

3rd ODI June 20 | MA Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai | 1:30 PM IST

What NRIs Need to Know

For diaspora fans in the United States, the Test starts at 12:00 AM EDT / 9:00 PM PDT on June 5 — a late-night affair for the East Coast, a prime-time watch party opportunity on the West Coast. The ODIs at 1:30 PM IST translate to 4:00 AM EDT / 1:00 AM PDT, which means early-morning cricket for American NRIs.

In the United Kingdom, the Test begins at 5:00 AM BST, while ODIs start at 9:00 AM BST — manageable for weekend matches, tougher for the midweek fixtures.

The series is seen as a crucial preparation window ahead of India’s packed schedule: the women’s T20 World Cup in England starts June 12, the men’s tour of England follows in July, and the FIFA World Cup runs concurrently from June 11. For cricket-first NRIs, the Afghanistan series offers a final, focused window of bilateral cricket before the calendar fragments.

The Bigger Picture

This tour is about more than results. It is about whether Gill can stamp authority on Test captaincy. It is about whether the Chandigarh crowd, starved of international cricket, will fill the new stadium. It is about whether Kohli and Rohit, playing together in ODIs with no World Cup pressure, can remind everyone why they are irreplaceable.

And for Afghanistan, it is about proving that their growth in world cricket is not a mirage. A competitive showing in India — in a Test, under lights in ODIs — would validate years of progress built in difficult circumstances.

Sources: BCCI, Afghanistan Cricket Board, ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz
